needs_transform.why: Supplier_Name does not reliably carry the registered name. About 44% of values have no brackets (e.g. 'Peoplebank Australia Limited', 'Shorewater Marine'), and in bracketed values the Pty Ltd registered name may sit outside the brackets (e.g. 'Thermo Fisher Australia Pty Ltd (Thermo Fisher Scientific Australia Pty Ltd)'). Deciding which part is the registered name, and which is the trading name, needs a transform that identifies the registered name from the text. No such transform exists, so entity.legal_name and entity.trading_name are not mapped from this column.

source_reliability_basis: WA Government statutory tender-award disclosure, published by the Department of Treasury and Finance. Strong for the fact that a contract was awarded to a named supplier. Supplier names and addresses are as entered by buying agencies (inconsistent casing, 'Trading (Legal)' mixes), so identity and address are rated below a statutory company register. Classification (UNSPSC) describes goods or services rather than supplier industry and is weak for entity classification. Contact is not provided by the source, so 0.5 is used as an uninformed default.

changes.what: Removed the entity.legal_name mapping from Supplier_Name (regex_extract of the parenthetical).
changes.why: Reviewer found the bracketed text is not always the registered name: the Pty Ltd name can sit outside the brackets, and 44% of names have no brackets. The parenthetical rule therefore assigns the wrong claim to legal_name. Rule 5 requires a consistent pattern before extracting, and none exists.

changes.what: Removed the entity.trading_name mapping from Supplier_Name (regex_extract of text before the parenthetical).
changes.why: Same defect: the text before the brackets is not reliably a trading name. Mapping it would publish a wrong trading name for many rows.

changes.what: Rewrote the needs_transform entry for Supplier_Name.
changes.why: The gap is no longer only the missing fallback for unbracketed names. The registered name cannot be identified from the text with the available transforms, so the column is needs_transform, not mapped.

changes.what: Kept entity.entity_type (entity_type_from_suffix), address.full, address.postcode, record_id, observed_at, valid_from, valid_to, and all unmapped entries unchanged.
changes.why: The reviewer did not flag these. The entity_type rule depends only on the suffix test, which remains valid for unbracketed names; bracketed names return unknown, which is the conservative default.

warning_responses.reason: The bracket-as-legal-name rule was wrong. Brackets are not always the legal name, and many registered names sit outside them. The field is removed from fields and Supplier_Name is listed in needs_transform until a transform can identify the registered name.

The text before the brackets is not reliably a trading name, because the registered name can be outside the brackets and 44% of names have no brackets. The field is removed from fields and Supplier_Name is listed in needs_transform.
